rows.title: Experienced Consultant
rows.descriptionText:
Apply now »

Experienced Consultant

Date: Sep 25, 2026

Location:

Washington DC- Onsite, DC, US

Company Brand: McLarens

Company Overview

KCIC is a consulting and technology firm specializing in risk management, litigation support, insurance analytics, and data-driven business solutions. Since 2002, KCIC has helped organizations navigate complex legal, financial, and operational challenges through a combination of industry expertise, advanced analytics, and innovative technology.The company is recognized for its work in mass tort litigation, product liability, asbestos, talc, PFAS, and other emerging risk areas. By leveraging proprietary technology platforms and deep analytical capabilities, KCIC helps clients gain actionable insights, improve decision-making, and effectively manage risk.

Headquartered in Washington, D.C., KCIC brings together consultants, data scientists, technologists, and subject matter experts who are committed to solving complex problems and delivering meaningful results. The company's collaborative approach and focus on innovation have established it as a trusted partner across a range of industries.

Key Accountabilities

 Partner with clients to solve complex litigation, claims, insurance, and business challenges

through data analysis, problem-solving, and thoughtful recommendations.

 Analyze and interpret large, complex datasets using SQL, Excel, Power BI, and other tools to

support reporting, forecasting, financial analyses, and client decision-making.

 Review, validate, and investigate data from claims, insurance policies, payments, and related

sources, identifying discrepancies and ensuring the accuracy and quality of client deliverables.

 Collaborate with clients, analysts, and software developers to understand business needs,

document requirements, test new functionality, and support the rollout of enhancements to

KCIC's technology platforms, including Ligado.

 Support ongoing improvements to Ligado by participating in user acceptance testing, gathering

user feedback, troubleshooting issues, maintaining documentation, and helping clients

effectively use the platform.

 Develop expertise in clients' businesses, litigation and claims management processes, insurance

coverage structures, and KCIC's consulting and technology offerings.

 Prepare and communicate analyses, reports, and recommendations to clients and colleagues,

clearly explaining methodologies, findings, risks, and proposed next steps.

 Manage multiple priorities across client projects, demonstrating strong organization, attention to

detail, sound judgment, and accountability for meeting deadlines and client expectations.

 Review work for accuracy and completeness, identify opportunities for improvement, and

contribute to solving complex client problems.

 Support the development of junior team members through training, knowledge sharing, and

day-to-day collaboration.

 Contribute to the growth of the firm through recruiting, training, thought leadership, and other

internal initiatives.

Experience And Qualifications

 Bachelor’s degree in an analytical or technical field such as business, data science, finance,

economics, or systems engineering. Master’s degree is a plus.

 2-3 years of post-graduation career experience Willing to work in the office 5 days per week, with future development into flexible, hybrid

opportunities

 Proficient knowledge of relational databases; proficient in Microsoft 365 suite (Word, Excel,

PowerPoint, Outlook), with a deep understanding of leveraging Excel for complex data analysis,

reporting, and automation. Familiarity with additional tools such as Power BI, VBA.

 Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, as well as communication and interpersonal

Skills

 Ability to work independently and within a collaborative, team-based environment Intellectually curious, motivated, and eager to learn Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to balance competing priorities and effectively

manage time to consistently meet deadlines.

Life at KCIC

Our people make KCIC the high-energy, high-performance, collaborative environment that it is. Those

who are new to the KCIC community bring innovative ideas, fresh perspectives, and the latest skills for

developing new technologies — all of which foster creative client solutions. We have developed an

environment where our employees feel confident to give voice to their ideas and are encouraged to take

ownership of their work. Our team is comprised of passionate individuals with diverse backgrounds,

including but not limited to business, systems engineering, data analytics, finance, and economics. At

KCIC, you will help solve some of the most complex problems and technical challenges that companies

face today.

KCIC is committed to creating a community where people can be their authentic selves. We embrace all

diversity, including race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, and religion in our KCIC community

and in our clients. Each consultant at KCIC understands the value of diversity and inclusion and that

diverse ideas can lead to unique, powerful solutions for our clients.

The workplace

Since 1932, we’ve been who people turn to in tough times. That’s a huge responsibility. It’s also a

huge opportunity. McLarens is a premier independent loss adjusting and forensic technical services

firm, with a global network that delivers consistently excellent service supported by deep local

expertise.

Our work spans industries and the globe. From disaster relief to aviation, engineering to natural

resources, our people get everything they need to impact lives on a global scale. We take our

development seriously and offer careers that empower our people to strive for bigger goals and

rows.title: Senior Associate, Data Scientist -  Operational Risk Management
rows.descriptionText:
Senior Associate, Data Scientist - Operational Risk Management

Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of records to unlock the big opportunities that help us manage risk so everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

Team Description

The Operational Risk Analytics, Innovation, and Reporting team owns and drives end-to-end data analysis and reporting of Capital One’s operational risk performance, delivering critical insights to Senior Executives and the Board. The team is responsible for the governance, monitoring, and analysis of operational risk data, as well as developing data-driven insights to inform strategic risk management decisions and practices. As a Senior Data Scientist you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption in risk data at a whole new scale. You will use the latest in computing and machine learning technologies to unlock the big opportunities that help drive efficiency and improve risk management, and you will do it all in a collaborative environment that values your insight, encourages you to take on new responsibility, promotes continuous learning, and rewards innovation. You will be the driving force to experiment, innovate, and create next-generation features powered by the latest emerging NLP and Generative AI technologies. If you love a fast-paced, highly rewarding environment, and you love being a builder and communicator, this is the place for you.

In this role, you will:

Partner with a cross-functional team of data scientists, software engineers, and product managers to deliver a product customers loveLeverage a broad stack of technologies — Python, Conda, AWS, H2O, Spark, and more — to reveal the insights hidden within huge volumes of numeric and textual dataBuild machine learning models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, validation, and implementationFlex your interpersonal skills to translate the complexity of your work into tangible business goals

The Ideal Candidate is:

Innovative. You continually research and evaluate emerging technologies. You stay current on published state-of-the-art methods, technologies, and applications and seek out opportunities to apply them. Creative. You thrive on bringing definition to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and pushing hard to find answers. You’re not afraid to share a new idea. Technical. You’re comfortable with open-source languages and are passionate about developing further. You have hands-on experience developing data science solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms. Statistically-minded. You’ve built models, validated them, and backtested them. You know how to interpret a confusion matrix or a ROC curve. You have experience with clustering, classification, sentiment analysis, time series, and deep learning. A data guru. “Big data” doesn’t faze you. You have the skills to retrieve, combine, and analyze data from a variety of sources and structures. You know understanding the data is often the key to great data science. 

Basic Qualifications:

Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining one of the following with an expectation that the required degree will be obtained on or before the scheduled start date:A Bachelor's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) plus 2 years of experience performing data analyticsA Master's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) or an MBA with a quantitative concentration
Preferred Qualifications: 

Master’s Degree in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics), or PhD in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics)Experience working with AWSAt least 2 years of experience in Python, Scala, or RAt least 2 years of experience with machine learningAt least 2 years of experience with SQL

rows.title: Senior Cost Accounting Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
JOB DESCRIPTION: 

Allied Technologies and Consulting (ATC) is recruiting for a Senior Cost Analyst with advanced level cost accounting and analysis in accordance with federal and agency regulations reporting to the Deputy Chief of Staff for Resource Management (DCSRM) within US Army Medical Research and Development Command (USAMRDC). This position is based in Frederick, MD, and will require up to 5 days on-site at either ATC’s Frederick office or at Fort Detrick. Approval for telework arrangements will be made on a case-by-case basis.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: 

Duties

The experienced, professional, and dynamic Senior Cost Analyst will assist with a variety of products and programs and perform the following duties:

Assist the DCSRM staff with transactional data input into GFEBS in the following functional areas: funds management and funds distribution; spending chain, pre-commitment processing, and out-going Military Interdepartmental Purchase Request (MIPR); reimbursable business process to include in-coming MIPR processing; Government Purchase Card (GPC) support; labor allocation; cost management business process; Project Systems/WBS elements in GFEBS. Generate management and financial reports in GFEBS to include but not limited to status of funds reports, open commitment reports, open obligation reports, and cost management reports. Review and analyze error reports in GFEBS to recommend corrections to include but not limited to interface monitor errors. Assist with implementing USAMRDC standardized cost models across all fund centers for indirect costs and ancillary/other direct cost capturing. The Contractor shall use the cost accounting models to develop appropriate pricing structures to recover the cost of product and services consumed by direct and reimbursable customers. Provide financial analysis support with extensive involvement in responses to requests as it relates to indirect cost and indirect rate analysis (revenue generated versus funds executed). Analysis of support agreements (interagency and interservice) and determining USAMRDC consumption levels per customer. Indirect rate revenue anticipated compared to actual indirect funds received and operational funds generated. This includes periodically reviews during the year to determine budget execution levels. Assist with development of dashboard components as it relates financial execution compared to Tables of Distribution and Allowances (TDA) requirements and authorizations. Various requests from customers (i.e., Congressional inquiries) for detailed analysis of how the USAMRDC indirect cost rates are developed and what services/activities are provided to support the funding. This requires the Contractor to be able to dissect the complex USAMRDC cost accounting by funding appropriation and then accumulation of the various funding into a logical response to the requesting agency. Provide training on capturing cost accounting data within GFEBS. The Contractor shall complete GFEBS specific Computer Based Training / Instructor Lead Train (CBT/ILT) courses to ensure proper provisioning of GFEBS cost management roles. Training includes hands-on for USAMRDC and subordinate units on GFEBS cost reports, how to extract data using GFEBS B and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) components, and how to interpret the data within those reports and recommend corrective actions if needed. Generate ad hoc reports using GFEBS or other USAMRDC approved software meeting the suspense date. Facilitate USAMRDC’s use of the cost accounting models to enhance organizational performance measurement for manpower surveys to establish reasonable performance targets based on the acceptable amount of resources needed to perform each activity established by the models. Review the USAMRDC cost accounting models and other information to conduct an in-depth analysis on the processes to identify opportunities for improvement and utilizing analysis techniques. Provide the link between process costs and customers to ensure appropriate cost recovery from reimbursable customers. Become the SME to answer cost accounting, GFEBS Cost Management and Cost Analysis related questions and provide assistance as requested. 

Education, Skills And Experience Required

Bachelor’s Degree preferred and/or two full years of progressively higher-level education leading to such a degree in the business or related field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the duties outlined in the job requirements OR combination of education and work experience. At least two years of experience utilizing an automated financial system such as General Fund Enterprise Business System (GFEBS) Specialized experience in the area of Federal appropriations law, Federal budget analysis and financial reporting, Army budget experience preferred. Proven experience in the field related to implementation of federal concepts, policies, and principles of budget. Experience with SAP BusinessObjects (BOBJ) Report Generation, Advanced Variable Creation & Automation and Complex Multi-Dimensional Layouts. Excellent communications, writing, organizational and project management skills. Sharepoint and experience desired. Experience, knowledge and the ability to execute using Microsoft Office Suite, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, as well as Microsoft Outlook. At least 2-3 years’ experience in Federal contracting, government or military environment is preferred. Travel up to 10% of the time may be required. Public Trust T1-NACI Clearance required. US Citizen Required. Must be able to pass background testing. THIS IS A FEDERAL CONTRACT.

About Ellucian

Ellucian powers innovation for higher education, partnering with approximately 3,000 customers across 50 countries, serving more than 21 million students. Ellucian's AI-powered platform, trained on the richest dataset available in higher education, drives efficiency, personalized experiences, and strengthened engagement for all students, faculty and staff. Fueled by decades of experience with a singular focus on the unique needs of learning institutions, the Ellucian platform features best-in-class SaaS capabilities and delivers insights needed now and into the future. These solutions and services span the entire student lifecycle, including data-rich tools for student recruitment, enrollment, and retention to workforce analytics, fundraising, and alumni engagement. Ellucian's innovative solutions, vast ecosystem of partners and user community of more than 45,000 provides best practices leading to greater institutional success and achieving better student outcomes.

About The Opportunity

Are you looking to join an innovative team at a leading higher education technology company? If you’re passionate about Support Operations analytics and eager to build expertise in business intelligence, enterprise support tools, and global customer support data strategy, this role is for you!

As part of Ellucian’s Global Support organization, you’ll develop data assets, dashboards, and operational insights that enable informed decision-making across technical support, operations, and leadership teams.

As the Business Intelligence Analyst for Global Support, you’ll use Tableau, ServiceNow, Excel, and automation tools to deliver accurate and timely reporting. Working closely with Support leaders, you’ll refine BI solutions that improve customer outcomes, strengthen operational discipline, and enable faster, more informed decisions.

Where You Will Make an Impact

Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting tools to help Global Support and business leaders understand operational trends, including backlog, SLA performance, MTTA, MTTR, escalation volume, and case aging.Analyze support data by developing hypotheses, documenting assumptions, and identifying trends, relationships, contributing factors, and opportunities for improvement.Partner with internal stakeholders to define business questions, determine appropriate analytical approaches, and translate findings into actionable insights and recommendations.Deliver high-quality analyses, reports, and presentations using clear, accessible visualizations for operational and leadership audiences.Identify opportunities to streamline and automate recurring reporting processes while maintaining the accuracy, reliability, and usability of dashboards and data assets.

What You Will Bring

3+ years of relevant experience in business intelligence, support operations analytics, customer or technical support analytics, or a related role involving reporting and operational analysis.Advanced Excel skills, including complex formulas, pivot tables, and analysis across multiple datasets; proficiency in PowerPoint.Experience with support or operations data, including case management, SLA performance, backlog, escalations, knowledge management, customer satisfaction, or related service delivery metrics.Experience building dashboards and generating insights using Tableau or a comparable business intelligence platform.Strong attention to detail, with a commitment to data accuracy, consistency, and reliable reporting maintenance.Ability to manage priorities independently, collaborate across teams, respond to time-sensitive needs, and constructively identify opportunities to improve existing approaches.Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to structure complex questions and translate findings into practical action.Working knowledge of data extraction, validation, analytical methods, and interpretation techniques.Strong communication, presentation, and data-storytelling skills, with the ability to explain findings to varied audiences.

Extra Credit

Experience with ServiceNow or another case-management platform.Interest in developing skills in predictive analytics, advanced analytics, or data science.

rows.title: Research Associate - Food, Nutrition, and Agriculture Program

company.name: The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine

rows.descriptionText:
Job Description Summary

ABOUT THE PROGRAM

The Food, Nutrition, and Agriculture program area convenes experts and leaders in food science, food safety, and food quality; nutrition and health; agricultural sciences and natural resources management to provide independent and cross-sector guidance to address a range of challenges in the food and agricultural system.

About The Opportunity

The Research Associate will support a team working on the project, "An Update of the Macronutrient Dietary Reference Intakes (DRIs)", last revised in 2005. The DRIs are quantitative nutrient reference values used to inform U.S. and Canadian food and nutrition programs, policies, regulations, and professional practice and are widely recognized as authoritative guidance on nutrient requirements and intake levels that support health and reduce chronic disease risk.

The Research Associate supports the project through research, analysis, technical writing, program coordination, and meeting-related activities. Responsibilities include managing literature reviews and reference libraries, analyzing data, developing background research, preparing background materials and reports, fact checking, and supporting committee activities.

Job Description

PLEASE NOTE A COVER LETTER IS REQUIRED FOR CONSIDERATION****

Responsibilities

RESEARCH

Conducts research and analysis to support the DRIs project.Identifies, evaluates, and synthesizes information from scientific literature, data sources, and other relevant materials.Develops research methodologies and prepares project outlines.Summarizes findings for reports, fact sheets, presentations, and other project deliverables.Verifies references and validates factual content in reports and supporting materials.Performs targeted literature searches and manages systematic literature searches and reference librariesAs appropriate, may conduct basic statistical analyses.

PROJECT AND MEETING ACTIVITIES

Works closely with senior staff, volunteer experts, sponsors, and external stakeholders to help ensure the successful execution of projects and convening activities, including expert workshops, committee meetings, webinars, and working groups from planning through dissemination.Prepares agendas, briefing materials, meeting summaries, and other technical documents; coordinates meeting logistics and speaker communications.Documents key discussions and action items; and assists with the development of meeting proceedings and other project deliverables.Maintains National Academies’ project databases, public access files, and project records in accordance with established procedures.Supports compliance with applicable policies and requirements, including the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) and Governing Board Project Approval Committee (GBPAC) processes, when applicable.

WRITING

Drafts, edits, and summarizes technical materials, reports, and background papers.Prepares tables and summaries from scientific literature and research findings for committee review.Reviews and edits materials prepared by committee members, consultants, and senior staff to ensure accuracy, consistency, and clarity.Incorporates feedback and revises documents to support high-quality publications and project deliverables.

DATABASE MANAGEMENT

Maintains bibliographic, analytical, and reference databases.Documents methodologies, statistical analyses, data sources, and supporting materials.Develops and maintains files related to project analyses and research activities.Prepares and formats databases to support data collection and reporting.

COMMUNICATION

As appropriate responds to inquiries from sponsors, scientific communities, stakeholders, and the public regarding assigned projects.Supports outreach efforts that increase awareness of committee studies and activities.Develops and maintains productive working relationships with professional organizations, advocacy groups, and subject matter experts.Shares knowledge and serves as a resource to colleagues. May mentor or provide guidance to junior staff.

Requirements

EDUCATION

Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and experience required. Master's degree in a related field preferred.

Required Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Knowledge of research methodologies, literature review techniques, and information analysis.

Ability to analyze complex information, synthesize findings, and communicate results clearly.Demonstrated critical thinking and sound judgment in solving a variety of research and program-related challenges.Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities and meeting deadlines.Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and standard research, database, and information management tools.Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise discretion when handling sensitive information.

Experience

Two years of related professional experience required.

COMMUNICATION AND TEAMWORK

Excellent communication skills with a proven ability to effectively interact with all levels of employees. Ability to work successfully in a team environment. Ability to develop relationships with co-workers and employees in other National Academies' departments through effective communication.

SUPERVISION

Reports to Senior Program Director and Senior Program Officer. Sets goals with supervisor.

Compensation & Benefits

An estimated compensation range for this position is $58,700 - $73,370. Compensation offered to the selected candidate will be based on the candidate’s relevant knowledge, skills, and work experience, commensurate with compensation of current employees in comparable positions with similar knowledge, skills, and work experience, and subject to budget parameters. Note it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at the higher end of the range. This is a benefits-eligible position. Our Benefits Plan offers competitive and comprehensive benefit options, including medical, dental and vision insurance, life insurance, disability coverage, retirement and savings benefits, leave benefits such as paid holidays and paid personal leave, transportation subsidies, and education assistance. For more information, please click here.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

Hybrid Office/Telecommute environment, expected onsite percentage 60%. Occasional travel between National Academies’ facilities and to off-site meeting/sponsor locations.

Any qualification to be considered equivalent, in lieu of stated minimum, requires the prior approval of the Office of Human Resources.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by employees assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. Some functions in this description may be specific to a particular unit of the National Academies and not applicable to other units.

We are seeking a Behavioral Management Technologist that supports the behavioral management program for Animal Research & Care at Johns Hopkins University. This role is responsible for overseeing and conducting positive reinforcement training, socialization, and enrichment evaluation with laboratory animals.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities

Implement and evaluate social housing, environmental enrichment, and positive reinforcement training; strategies with various laboratory animal species.Assist with the assessment and monitoring of the psychological welfare of laboratory animals.Responsible for conducting positive reinforcement training of nonhuman primates and other large animal species for cooperation with common experimental and veterinary procedures.Design and document animal training plans; communicate training progress and program goals to faculty and staff as needed.Communicate, understand, and relay relevant research, behavioral, and veterinary medical terminology.Guide the social housing of laboratory housed animals, including forming social pairs, assessing behavioral compatibility between animals, and monitoring the stability of socially housed animals in pairs and groups.Assist with the design and implementation of enrichment devices for various laboratory animal species. Assists with evaluating the efficacy of the environmental enhancement plan for laboratory housed animals.Maintain accurate behavioral records and regulatory documents.Maintain research equipment and initiates the process for equipment repair when needed.Communicate with faculty and staff in a timely and professional manner when issues arise with research plans or deadlines to determine solutions.Provide administrative support and other duties as assigned.

At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

Department Summary:

The Market Intelligence and Research team

MITRE is seeking a curious and collaborative early career Research Analyst, Research Associate, Information Professional, or Librarian to join our Research Services team, a part of MITRE’s Market Intelligence & Research organization. This individual will be responsible for providing, locating, gathering, and analyzing information from third-parties, open-source news and articles, published research papers, subscription and public databases and other sources in support of MITRE’s work programs, and specific sponsor and MITRE initiatives.

As a research associate, this key team member will need a growing understanding and/or interest in databases, digital research libraries, query techniques and short cuts, research and information management practices, and OS intelligence platforms (news alerts, dashboards). This role focuses on desk research, secondary research, literature searching/review, open-source and subscription-based research, and synthesis of existing information for internal clients. This is not a primary research, laboratory, engineering, scientific, or product research role.

This role will translate internal client questions into tangible research objectives to meet the needs of our customers and will engage with internal clients to scope and prioritize tasks, collecting and working with a variety of research outputs, and performing additional desk and secondary research as necessary. This position supports other department capabilities in business analyses, strategy, and sponsor and market intelligence as needed. This role will interact with all levels of the company, including senior level managers, technical SMEs, and analysts.

The ideal candidate is intellectually curious, highly motivated to find answers, and eager to develop a consultative approach to research support by helping clients refine questions, identify the most relevant sources, and shape actionable outputs. The ideal candidate will have interest in performing research on a broad range of topics, an entrepreneurial approach to generating and creating value and impact, and an appreciation for a nonprofit/public interest environment.

rows.title: Investigator
rows.descriptionText:
Job Summary

This position is in the Office of the Inspector General (OIG), Risk Assessment and Future Planning Unit (RAFP). The OIG's mission is to promote economy, efficiency, and effectiveness and to detect and deter fraud, waste, and abuse in District government programs and operations. RAFP is responsible for evaluating its risks and assisting OIG in making proactive, knowledge-driven decisions.

The incumbent is responsible for assisting and conducting preliminary inquiries and/or investigations of possible violations involving federal and District of Columbia laws and regulations. The results of those inquiries/investigations are presented to the responsible official(s) for appropriate action.

Duties And Responsibilities

Intakes, processes, and analyzes complaints made to the OIG fraud hotline. Inputs data into agency data systems, provides written and verbal correspondence with the public, conducts interviews, and synthesizes data from multiple sources to draw logical and reasonable conclusions; maintains confidentiality, executes proper course of action for each complaint, and presents recommendations of corresponding actions to agency leadership. Conduct interviews with complainants and government officials to obtain all required information, determine potential issues, and identify potential violations of Federal and District laws, policies, and regulations.

Plans and conducts complete administrative investigations of a wide variety of employee misconduct, including procurement and contract irregularities, conflicts of interest, and violations of District code, personnel manual, ethics violations, and District agency policies. Examines records, books, payrolls, reports, correspondence, and other data of consequence related to transactions, actions, or allegations under investigation. Verifies and corroborates all information obtained, presented, or alleged to establish accuracy and authenticity of facts and/or evidence. Conduct interviews with witnesses and subjects of investigations to present findings in comprehensive reports of investigation.

Manipulates, manages, queries, analyzes, and summarizes data from open source, law enforcement, District, and OIG data sources into cohesive reports in support of investigations, audits, and inspections of fraud, waste, and abuse that can be found in the form of a database, financial records, expense reports, emails, and other formats. Performs quality control tasks on data sets created. Performs research to identify and obtain data when necessary to meet agency data analysis needs.

Performs other related duties as assigned

Qualifications And Education

Applicants must have one year of specialized experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the CS-9 grade level, or its non-District equivalent. Specialized experience for this position includes: assisting and conducting preliminary inquiries and/or investigations of possible violations involving federal and District of Columbia laws and regulations. The results of those inquiries/investigations are presented to the responsible official(s) for appropriate action. Routine duties that justify this position’s security sensitive suitability include manipulating, managing, and summarizing data from open source, law enforcement, District, and OIG data sources into cohesive reports in support of investigations, audits, and inspections of fraud, waste, and abuse that can be found in the form of a database, financial records, expense reports, emails, and other formats. Additionally, the investigator will perform quality control tasks on data sets created; research to identify and obtain data when necessary to meet agency data analysis needs.

This position prefers incumbent be a graduate of a 4-year accredited college or university.

At least two years of experience in investigative procedures, compliance or human resources or an equivalent combination of experience and education

Work Environment

Work is primarily performed in an office setting (or cubicle), and the work area is adequately lighted, heated, and ventilated. Travel to external site visits, interviews, court appearances, training, and meetings may be required on a limited and inconsistent basis.

Other Significant Facts

Promotion Potential: No known promotion

Duration of Appointment: Career Service Appointment

Pay Plan, Series and Grade: CS-1810-11

Salary range: $65,285 - $84,167 (Capped 11/4)

The position may be filled at salary up to a Step 4.

This position is not represented by a collective bargaining unit.

The incumbent of this position will be subject to enhanced suitability screening pursuant to Chapter 4 of D.C. personnel regulations, Suitability- Security Sensitive.

This position has been designated as a security sensitive position. Security sensitive positions are positions of special trust that may be reasonably expected to affect the access to or control of activities, systems, or resources that are subject to misappropriation, malicious mischief, damage, or loss or impairment of control of communication.

Submission of a resume alone is NOT a complete application. This position may require the completion of additional form/s and/or supplemental materials. Failure to provide the required information and/or materials will result in your application not being considered for employment.

Mental Health Clinician (LGPC/LMSW) 

About The Role 

Join our clinician-centered multidisciplinary team in Columbia, MD, and grow your career alongside counselors, social workers, and psychologists. At Ellie Mental Health, we prioritize clinician well-being so our team can provide exceptional care. Clinicians receive flexible scheduling, health insurance, paid time off, free CEUs, weekly case consultation groups, and regular team activities focused on wellness and connection.

We are seeking full-time Maryland Licensed Graduate Professional Counselors (LGPCs) and Licensed Master Social Workers (LMSWs) interested in gaining post-graduate clinical experience. Paid supervision is included.

We value clinicians who enjoy collaboration, bring a sense of humor to their work, and are committed to serving clients from diverse backgrounds.

Complete clinical documentation, including progress notes and treatment updates. Provide high-quality, client-centered care. Coordinate services with other providers as needed. Experience with assessments, treatment planning, and clinical documentation. Commitment to LGBTQIA+ affirming, culturally responsive care. Dedication to lifelong learning, cultural humility, and ethical practice. Bilingual clinicians are strongly encouraged to apply. 

Benefits 

Competitive hourly compensation. Paid supervision and professional development. Flexible scheduling. Health insurance. Paid time off. Free CEU library and ongoing training opportunities. Career growth and leadership development pathways. Flexibility to work with populations and treatment approaches that match your interests, including children, adolescents, adults, couples, groups, and play therapy. 

About Ellie Mental Health 

Founded by clinicians in 2015, Ellie Mental Health was created to reduce administrative burdens and help therapists focus on client care. We provide centralized administrative support, competitive compensation, training, and flexibility so clinicians can thrive professionally and personally.

Equal Opportunity Employer 

Independent Ellie Mental Health franchisees are Equal Opportunity Employers committed to fostering diverse and inclusive workplaces. Employment decisions are made by the independently owned and operated franchise location.

Flexible work from home options available.

Seeking creative & collaborative humans with a passion for changing mental health care in fun and meaningful ways.

Don’t meet EVERY requirement?

Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. Ellie Mental Health is devoted to purposefully building an inclusive and diverse workplace where all of our humans can be their authentic selves! (Authenticity is one of our core values, after all…) If you’re excited about the chance to be a change-maker with us, but your past experience doesn’t perfectly align with every single qualification of the job description, we encourage you to apply anyways. Our mental health jobs need dedicated individuals from every background who are willing to care for others. And who knows, you might just be the perfect candidate for another role!

Employee Experience

We take care of our people. It’s that simple. From investing in their financial future, to providing wages that shatter the ceiling in our industry to reasonable caseload expectations we ensure that our people are happy. Happy employees do better work and provide better client care! No matter what it is that you do in your mental health career at Ellie, our clients depend on us cultivating an environment where our employees can thrive so that they can thrive too!

Y’all, jobs in mental health are tough jobs with a high risk of emotional fatigue and burnout. At Ellie, we use all of our core values of humor, creativity, authenticity, acceptance, determination, and compassion not just out in our communities, but we turn them inwards too! Our employees have clear growth paths for advancing their careers.

We have created a culture that reminds us that our employees are our leaders!

Company Structure

Ellie is a socially responsible for-profit business, which allows us to be flexible and responsive to our community’s needs. Many mental health and wellness-focused companies are non-profits or government agencies, which rely on the general public, grants, or large donors for funding. This model often results in little creativity and lower compensation for employees, promoting a work culture that just makes people feel “blah.”

Feeling blah doesn’t help employees stay motivated, engaged, or even in their jobs for a very long time! So we created a new model: one that puts flexibility, innovative decision-making, creativity, and our people first, while remaining a socially conscious and responsible for-profit business focused on changing how we treat mental health.

In short, we’re just people helping people. Wanna join the herd?

rows.title: Operations Research Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Overview

Systems Planning and Analysis, Inc. (SPA) delivers high-impact, technical solutions to complex national security issues. With over 50 years of business expertise and consistent growth, we are known for continuous innovation for our government customers, in both the US and abroad. Our exceptionally talented team is highly collaborative in spirit and practice, producing Results that Matter . Come work with the best! We offer opportunity, unique challenges, and clear-sighted commitment to the mission. SPA: Objective. Responsive. Trusted.

We’re seeking a highly motivated Operations Research Analyst to support key DoD programs in the National Capital Region. In this role, you will apply advanced analytic techniques, modeling and simulation tools, and clear communication skills to help senior decision‑makers evaluate complex defense challenges. The ideal candidate brings strong quantitative expertise, hands‑on experience with data‑driven analysis, and the ability to thrive in a collaborative, fast‑paced environment requiring the candidate to obtain a Top Secret/SCI eligibility.

SPA has a near-term need for an Operations Research Analyst. #KS

Responsibilities

The successful candidate will contribute to project teams by building digital models, running simulations, analyzing complex data, and supporting clear communication of results. Day-to-day work includes the ability to:

 Develop digital models of complex real-world systems using commercial and proprietary tools.  Design, build, and execute constructive simulations using best practices for design of experiments.  Analyze and synthesize large data sets using diverse analytic frameworks and statistical methods.  Prepare presentations, reports, and other deliverables to convey findings and recommendations.  Balance tasks across multiple projects and maintain regular communication with task leads. 

Qualifications

This position supports DoD programs in the National Capital Region and requires strong analytic, technical, and communication skills to inform decision‑making across complex defense challenges. The main office is located at the SPA Main HQ building in Alexandria, VA

Required Qualifications

 Bachelor’s degree in Operations Research, Mathematics, Engineering, Data Science, or a closely related field  At least two years of professional experience in operations research, modeling and simulation, or model‑based systems engineering  Demonstrated proficiency in data analysis and visualization using Excel, Python, R, Tableau, or other tools  Proven ability to apply structured, rigorous analytic methodologies to complex problem-solving  Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to deliver clear technical presentations  An active or recent DoD security clearance 

Desired Qualifications

 Experience supporting DoD organizations, acquisition programs, or capability development activities  Familiarity with modeling and simulation tools commonly used in defense analysis (e.g., CAMEO, AFSIM, STK, AnyLogic) or mission-level modeling and simulation  Knowledge of design of experiments, statistical modeling, or machine learning methods 

 Pay Range Information 

At SPA, we strive to deliver a robust total compensation package that will attract and retain top talent. rows.descriptionText:
About Ellucian

Ellucian powers innovation for higher education, partnering with approximately 3,000 customers across 50 countries, serving more than 21 million students. Ellucian's AI-powered platform, trained on the richest dataset available in higher education, drives efficiency, personalized experiences, and strengthened engagement for all students, faculty and staff. Fueled by decades of experience with a singular focus on the unique needs of learning institutions, the Ellucian platform features best-in-class SaaS capabilities and delivers insights needed now and into the future. These solutions and services span the entire student lifecycle, including data-rich tools for student recruitment, enrollment, and retention to workforce analytics, fundraising, and alumni engagement. Ellucian's innovative solutions, vast ecosystem of partners and user community of more than 45,000 provides best practices leading to greater institutional success and achieving better student outcomes.

About The Opportunity

Are you looking to join an innovative team at a leading higher education technology company? If you’re passionate about Support Operations analytics and eager to build expertise in business intelligence, enterprise support tools, and global customer support data strategy, this role is for you!

As part of Ellucian’s Global Support organization, you’ll develop data assets, dashboards, and operational insights that enable informed decision-making across technical support, operations, and leadership teams.

As the Business Intelligence Analyst for Global Support, you’ll use Tableau, ServiceNow, Excel, and automation tools to deliver accurate and timely reporting. Working closely with Support leaders, you’ll refine BI solutions that improve customer outcomes, strengthen operational discipline, and enable faster, more informed decisions.

Where You Will Make an Impact

Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting tools to help Global Support and business leaders understand operational trends, including backlog, SLA performance, MTTA, MTTR, escalation volume, and case aging.Analyze support data by developing hypotheses, documenting assumptions, and identifying trends, relationships, contributing factors, and opportunities for improvement.Partner with internal stakeholders to define business questions, determine appropriate analytical approaches, and translate findings into actionable insights and recommendations.Deliver high-quality analyses, reports, and presentations using clear, accessible visualizations for operational and leadership audiences.Identify opportunities to streamline and automate recurring reporting processes while maintaining the accuracy, reliability, and usability of dashboards and data assets.

What You Will Bring

3+ years of relevant experience in business intelligence, support operations analytics, customer or technical support analytics, or a related role involving reporting and operational analysis.Advanced Excel skills, including complex formulas, pivot tables, and analysis across multiple datasets; proficiency in PowerPoint.Experience with support or operations data, including case management, SLA performance, backlog, escalations, knowledge management, customer satisfaction, or related service delivery metrics.Experience building dashboards and generating insights using Tableau or a comparable business intelligence platform.Strong attention to detail, with a commitment to data accuracy, consistency, and reliable reporting maintenance.Ability to manage priorities independently, collaborate across teams, respond to time-sensitive needs, and constructively identify opportunities to improve existing approaches.Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to structure complex questions and translate findings into practical action.Working knowledge of data extraction, validation, analytical methods, and interpretation techniques.Strong communication, presentation, and data-storytelling skills, with the ability to explain findings to varied audiences.

Extra Credit

Experience with ServiceNow or another case-management platform.Interest in developing skills in predictive analytics, advanced analytics, or data science.

rows.title: Research Associate - Food, Nutrition, and Agriculture Program

company.name: The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine

rows.descriptionText:
Job Description Summary

ABOUT THE PROGRAM

The Food, Nutrition, and Agriculture program area convenes experts and leaders in food science, food safety, and food quality; nutrition and health; agricultural sciences and natural resources management to provide independent and cross-sector guidance to address a range of challenges in the food and agricultural system.

About The Opportunity

The Research Associate will support a team working on the project, "An Update of the Macronutrient Dietary Reference Intakes (DRIs)", last revised in 2005. The DRIs are quantitative nutrient reference values used to inform U.S. and Canadian food and nutrition programs, policies, regulations, and professional practice and are widely recognized as authoritative guidance on nutrient requirements and intake levels that support health and reduce chronic disease risk.

The Research Associate supports the project through research, analysis, technical writing, program coordination, and meeting-related activities. Responsibilities include managing literature reviews and reference libraries, analyzing data, developing background research, preparing background materials and reports, fact checking, and supporting committee activities.

Job Description

PLEASE NOTE A COVER LETTER IS REQUIRED FOR CONSIDERATION****

Responsibilities

RESEARCH

Conducts research and analysis to support the DRIs project.Identifies, evaluates, and synthesizes information from scientific literature, data sources, and other relevant materials.Develops research methodologies and prepares project outlines.Summarizes findings for reports, fact sheets, presentations, and other project deliverables.Verifies references and validates factual content in reports and supporting materials.Performs targeted literature searches and manages systematic literature searches and reference librariesAs appropriate, may conduct basic statistical analyses.

PROJECT AND MEETING ACTIVITIES

Works closely with senior staff, volunteer experts, sponsors, and external stakeholders to help ensure the successful execution of projects and convening activities, including expert workshops, committee meetings, webinars, and working groups from planning through dissemination.Prepares agendas, briefing materials, meeting summaries, and other technical documents; coordinates meeting logistics and speaker communications.Documents key discussions and action items; and assists with the development of meeting proceedings and other project deliverables.Maintains National Academies’ project databases, public access files, and project records in accordance with established procedures.Supports compliance with applicable policies and requirements, including the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) and Governing Board Project Approval Committee (GBPAC) processes, when applicable.

WRITING

Drafts, edits, and summarizes technical materials, reports, and background papers.Prepares tables and summaries from scientific literature and research findings for committee review.Reviews and edits materials prepared by committee members, consultants, and senior staff to ensure accuracy, consistency, and clarity.Incorporates feedback and revises documents to support high-quality publications and project deliverables.

DATABASE MANAGEMENT

Maintains bibliographic, analytical, and reference databases.Documents methodologies, statistical analyses, data sources, and supporting materials.Develops and maintains files related to project analyses and research activities.Prepares and formats databases to support data collection and reporting.

COMMUNICATION

As appropriate responds to inquiries from sponsors, scientific communities, stakeholders, and the public regarding assigned projects.Supports outreach efforts that increase awareness of committee studies and activities.Develops and maintains productive working relationships with professional organizations, advocacy groups, and subject matter experts.Shares knowledge and serves as a resource to colleagues. May mentor or provide guidance to junior staff.

Requirements

EDUCATION

Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and experience required. Master's degree in a related field preferred.

Required Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Knowledge of research methodologies, literature review techniques, and information analysis.

Ability to analyze complex information, synthesize findings, and communicate results clearly.Demonstrated critical thinking and sound judgment in solving a variety of research and program-related challenges.Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities and meeting deadlines.Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and standard research, database, and information management tools.Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise discretion when handling sensitive information.

Experience

Two years of related professional experience required.

COMMUNICATION AND TEAMWORK

Excellent communication skills with a proven ability to effectively interact with all levels of employees. Ability to work successfully in a team environment. Ability to develop relationships with co-workers and employees in other National Academies' departments through effective communication.

SUPERVISION

Reports to Senior Program Director and Senior Program Officer. Sets goals with supervisor.

Compensation & Benefits

An estimated compensation range for this position is $58,700 - $73,370. Compensation offered to the selected candidate will be based on the candidate’s relevant knowledge, skills, and work experience, commensurate with compensation of current employees in comparable positions with similar knowledge, skills, and work experience, and subject to budget parameters. Note it is not typical for a candidate to be hired at the higher end of the range. This is a benefits-eligible position. Our Benefits Plan offers competitive and comprehensive benefit options, including medical, dental and vision insurance, life insurance, disability coverage, retirement and savings benefits, leave benefits such as paid holidays and paid personal leave, transportation subsidies, and education assistance. For more information, please click here.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

Hybrid Office/Telecommute environment, expected onsite percentage 60%. Occasional travel between National Academies’ facilities and to off-site meeting/sponsor locations.

Any qualification to be considered equivalent, in lieu of stated minimum, requires the prior approval of the Office of Human Resources.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by employees assigned to this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of personnel so classified. Some functions in this description may be specific to a particular unit of the National Academies and not applicable to other units.

rows.descriptionText:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

Department Summary:

The Market Intelligence and Research team

MITRE is seeking a curious and collaborative early career Research Analyst, Research Associate, Information Professional, or Librarian to join our Research Services team, a part of MITRE’s Market Intelligence & Research organization. This individual will be responsible for providing, locating, gathering, and analyzing information from third-parties, open-source news and articles, published research papers, subscription and public databases and other sources in support of MITRE’s work programs, and specific sponsor and MITRE initiatives.

As a research associate, this key team member will need a growing understanding and/or interest in databases, digital research libraries, query techniques and short cuts, research and information management practices, and OS intelligence platforms (news alerts, dashboards). This role focuses on desk research, secondary research, literature searching/review, open-source and subscription-based research, and synthesis of existing information for internal clients. This is not a primary research, laboratory, engineering, scientific, or product research role.

rows.title: Senior Cost Accounting Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
JOB DESCRIPTION: 

Allied Technologies and Consulting (ATC) is recruiting for a Senior Cost Analyst with advanced level cost accounting and analysis in accordance with federal and agency regulations reporting to the Deputy Chief of Staff for Resource Management (DCSRM) within US Army Medical Research and Development Command (USAMRDC). This position is based in Frederick, MD, and will require up to 5 days on-site at either ATC’s Frederick office or at Fort Detrick. Approval for telework arrangements will be made on a case-by-case basis.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: 

Duties

The experienced, professional, and dynamic Senior Cost Analyst will assist with a variety of products and programs and perform the following duties:

Assist the DCSRM staff with transactional data input into GFEBS in the following functional areas: funds management and funds distribution; spending chain, pre-commitment processing, and out-going Military Interdepartmental Purchase Request (MIPR); reimbursable business process to include in-coming MIPR processing; Government Purchase Card (GPC) support; labor allocation; cost management business process; Project Systems/WBS elements in GFEBS. Generate management and financial reports in GFEBS to include but not limited to status of funds reports, open commitment reports, open obligation reports, and cost management reports. Review and analyze error reports in GFEBS to recommend corrections to include but not limited to interface monitor errors. Assist with implementing USAMRDC standardized cost models across all fund centers for indirect costs and ancillary/other direct cost capturing. The Contractor shall use the cost accounting models to develop appropriate pricing structures to recover the cost of product and services consumed by direct and reimbursable customers. Provide financial analysis support with extensive involvement in responses to requests as it relates to indirect cost and indirect rate analysis (revenue generated versus funds executed). Analysis of support agreements (interagency and interservice) and determining USAMRDC consumption levels per customer. Indirect rate revenue anticipated compared to actual indirect funds received and operational funds generated. This includes periodically reviews during the year to determine budget execution levels. Assist with development of dashboard components as it relates financial execution compared to Tables of Distribution and Allowances (TDA) requirements and authorizations. Various requests from customers (i.e., Congressional inquiries) for detailed analysis of how the USAMRDC indirect cost rates are developed and what services/activities are provided to support the funding. This requires the Contractor to be able to dissect the complex USAMRDC cost accounting by funding appropriation and then accumulation of the various funding into a logical response to the requesting agency. Provide training on capturing cost accounting data within GFEBS. The Contractor shall complete GFEBS specific Computer Based Training / Instructor Lead Train (CBT/ILT) courses to ensure proper provisioning of GFEBS cost management roles. Training includes hands-on for USAMRDC and subordinate units on GFEBS cost reports, how to extract data using GFEBS B and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) components, and how to interpret the data within those reports and recommend corrective actions if needed. Generate ad hoc reports using GFEBS or other USAMRDC approved software meeting the suspense date. Facilitate USAMRDC’s use of the cost accounting models to enhance organizational performance measurement for manpower surveys to establish reasonable performance targets based on the acceptable amount of resources needed to perform each activity established by the models. Review the USAMRDC cost accounting models and other information to conduct an in-depth analysis on the processes to identify opportunities for improvement and utilizing analysis techniques. Provide the link between process costs and customers to ensure appropriate cost recovery from reimbursable customers. Become the SME to answer cost accounting, GFEBS Cost Management and Cost Analysis related questions and provide assistance as requested. 

Education, Skills And Experience Required

Bachelor’s Degree preferred and/or two full years of progressively higher-level education leading to such a degree in the business or related field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the duties outlined in the job requirements OR combination of education and work experience. At least two years of experience utilizing an automated financial system such as General Fund Enterprise Business System (GFEBS) Specialized experience in the area of Federal appropriations law, Federal budget analysis and financial reporting, Army budget experience preferred. Proven experience in the field related to implementation of federal concepts, policies, and principles of budget. Experience with SAP BusinessObjects (BOBJ) Report Generation, Advanced Variable Creation & Automation and Complex Multi-Dimensional Layouts. Excellent communications, writing, organizational and project management skills. Sharepoint and experience desired. Experience, knowledge and the ability to execute using Microsoft Office Suite, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, as well as Microsoft Outlook. At least 2-3 years’ experience in Federal contracting, government or military environment is preferred. Travel up to 10% of the time may be required. Public Trust T1-NACI Clearance required. US Citizen Required. Must be able to pass background testing. THIS IS A FEDERAL CONTRACT.

rows.title: Investigator
rows.descriptionText:
Job Summary

This position is in the Office of the Inspector General (OIG), Risk Assessment and Future Planning Unit (RAFP). The OIG's mission is to promote economy, efficiency, and effectiveness and to detect and deter fraud, waste, and abuse in District government programs and operations. RAFP is responsible for evaluating its risks and assisting OIG in making proactive, knowledge-driven decisions.

The incumbent is responsible for assisting and conducting preliminary inquiries and/or investigations of possible violations involving federal and District of Columbia laws and regulations. The results of those inquiries/investigations are presented to the responsible official(s) for appropriate action.

Duties And Responsibilities

Intakes, processes, and analyzes complaints made to the OIG fraud hotline. Inputs data into agency data systems, provides written and verbal correspondence with the public, conducts interviews, and synthesizes data from multiple sources to draw logical and reasonable conclusions; maintains confidentiality, executes proper course of action for each complaint, and presents recommendations of corresponding actions to agency leadership. Conduct interviews with complainants and government officials to obtain all required information, determine potential issues, and identify potential violations of Federal and District laws, policies, and regulations.

Plans and conducts complete administrative investigations of a wide variety of employee misconduct, including procurement and contract irregularities, conflicts of interest, and violations of District code, personnel manual, ethics violations, and District agency policies. Examines records, books, payrolls, reports, correspondence, and other data of consequence related to transactions, actions, or allegations under investigation. Verifies and corroborates all information obtained, presented, or alleged to establish accuracy and authenticity of facts and/or evidence. Conduct interviews with witnesses and subjects of investigations to present findings in comprehensive reports of investigation.

Manipulates, manages, queries, analyzes, and summarizes data from open source, law enforcement, District, and OIG data sources into cohesive reports in support of investigations, audits, and inspections of fraud, waste, and abuse that can be found in the form of a database, financial records, expense reports, emails, and other formats. Performs quality control tasks on data sets created. Performs research to identify and obtain data when necessary to meet agency data analysis needs.

Performs other related duties as assigned

Qualifications And Education

Applicants must have one year of specialized experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the CS-9 grade level, or its non-District equivalent. Specialized experience for this position includes: assisting and conducting preliminary inquiries and/or investigations of possible violations involving federal and District of Columbia laws and regulations. The results of those inquiries/investigations are presented to the responsible official(s) for appropriate action. Routine duties that justify this position’s security sensitive suitability include manipulating, managing, and summarizing data from open source, law enforcement, District, and OIG data sources into cohesive reports in support of investigations, audits, and inspections of fraud, waste, and abuse that can be found in the form of a database, financial records, expense reports, emails, and other formats. Additionally, the investigator will perform quality control tasks on data sets created; research to identify and obtain data when necessary to meet agency data analysis needs.

This position prefers incumbent be a graduate of a 4-year accredited college or university.

At least two years of experience in investigative procedures, compliance or human resources or an equivalent combination of experience and education

Work Environment

Work is primarily performed in an office setting (or cubicle), and the work area is adequately lighted, heated, and ventilated. Travel to external site visits, interviews, court appearances, training, and meetings may be required on a limited and inconsistent basis.

Other Significant Facts

Promotion Potential: No known promotion

Duration of Appointment: Career Service Appointment

Pay Plan, Series and Grade: CS-1810-11

Salary range: $65,285 - $84,167 (Capped 11/4)

The position may be filled at salary up to a Step 4.

This position is not represented by a collective bargaining unit.

The incumbent of this position will be subject to enhanced suitability screening pursuant to Chapter 4 of D.C. personnel regulations, Suitability- Security Sensitive.

This position has been designated as a security sensitive position. Security sensitive positions are positions of special trust that may be reasonably expected to affect the access to or control of activities, systems, or resources that are subject to misappropriation, malicious mischief, damage, or loss or impairment of control of communication.

Submission of a resume alone is NOT a complete application. This position may require the completion of additional form/s and/or supplemental materials. Failure to provide the required information and/or materials will result in your application not being considered for employment.

This role is responsible for designing clustering pipelines, building facet extraction workflows, and producing actionable intelligence on how users interact with chat systems. The Data Scientist works closely with engineers and stakeholders to surface usage patterns, identify emerging topics, and inform product decisions through data. Develop facet extraction approaches using LLMs to categorize conversations by request type, task performed, and topic discussed      - Build dashboards and reporting artifacts that communicate usage trends, emerging topics, and user behavior to stakeholders      - Department Summary:

The Market Intelligence and Research team

MITRE is seeking a curious and collaborative early career Research Analyst, Research Associate, Information Professional, or Librarian to join our Research Services team, a part of MITRE’s Market Intelligence & Research organization. This individual will be responsible for providing, locating, gathering, and analyzing information from third-parties, open-source news and articles, published research papers, subscription and public databases and other sources in support of MITRE’s work programs, and specific sponsor and MITRE initiatives.

As a research associate, this key team member will need a growing understanding and/or interest in databases, digital research libraries, query techniques and short cuts, research and information management practices, and OS intelligence platforms (news alerts, dashboards). This role focuses on desk research, secondary research, literature searching/review, open-source and subscription-based research, and synthesis of existing information for internal clients. This role will translate internal client questions into tangible research objectives to meet the needs of our customers and will engage with internal clients to scope and prioritize tasks, collecting and working with a variety of research outputs, and performing additional desk and secondary research as necessary. Wash World Copenhagen Metropolitan Area

Data Scientist

Wash World Copenhagen Metropolitan Area

About Wash World

Wash World runs more than 200 automatic car wash halls in Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Germany, and washed over 4 million cars in 2025. Every hall has cameras, sensors and payment terminals, so a lot of operational data comes in every day. We want to use that data to find faults in the wash machines automatically.

Who You'll Work With

You will work from our office in Copenhagen Ø, as part of the development team: three developers, two IT operations staff and one data analyst. Because the team is small, you will work directly with the people who run the systems you build on, and decisions get made quickly.

You will own your projects from your first week, including the choice of tools and models that suit the problem. As data and ML work at Wash World grows, you will have the opportunity to grow into the lead role for the area.

How We Build

AI coding agents are at the centre of how we work. We use them every day to write, test and ship code across the stack, and you will do the same, from data pipelines and database migrations to model training and deployment. We expect you to know how to work with agents well. That means giving them the right context, splitting work into tasks they can handle, and reviewing and testing what they produce before it ships. The code is still yours, and you are responsible for it.

Your impact

As a Data Scientist at Wash World, you will use camera footage, customer feedback and operational data to detect faults in our wash machines. You will also build and run the systems that put this into production.

Your main project is computer vision on hall footage, detecting problems with brushes, dryers, foam, high pressure and car positioning. Part of the work is finding out which approach works. That may mean evaluating vision-language models, or curating a proper labelled dataset and training a dedicated classifier. Either way, good labels come first: you will combine customer complaints, customer service reviews and technician reports into training and evaluation datasets, and check that each label means what it appears to.

You will also work on the data underneath. That includes restructuring MySQL and PostgreSQL schemas, writing safe migrations, tuning queries and keeping production data in sync with BigQuery. You will deploy and operate your own work on Google Cloud, and help the rest of the development team where your skills fit.

Our current stack is Laravel (PHP) and Node.js/TypeScript for production services and Python for machine learning, with MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis and BigQuery, running on Google Cloud (Cloud Run, GKE, Cloud Storage and Cloud Build).

Your Qualifications And Skills

A bachelor's, master's or PhD in data science, computer science, machine learning or a related field. Recent graduates are welcome, and so are candidates with up to 4 years of experience. Bachelor's students may be considered if they have additional entrepreneurial experience or supporting details.Hands-on experience building software with AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, ideally on more than small scripts. You know how to set them up with project instructions and tools, when to trust their output, and how to check it.Experience applying machine learning or computer vision to real-world data. A thesis or project counts.Strong SQL and a solid understanding of relational database design, including keys, indexing, normalisation and migrations in PostgreSQL and/or MySQLProgramming experience in at least one of PHP (Laravel / Slim), Python or TypeScript (Node.js)Experience with Docker and with deploying something to the cloud yourself, preferably on GCP. A personal or university project is fine.Ability to own a problem from start to finish, and to say clearly when something cannot work, for example when a camera cannot see a faultGood written and spoken English. Danish is not required, but knowledge of the language is an advantage.

Also valued: Kubernetes and Terraform, CI/CD, video tooling (ffmpeg, RTSP) and NVR/VMS systems, vision-language models and fine-tuning, self-hosted inference, Redis caching and pub/sub, BigQuery or dbt, and experience handling personal data under GDPR.

Hiring process

We will first conduct a virtual interview to determine whether there is a good fit. Then you will be invited to the office to conduct a follow-up interview and talk to the team if applicable.
